name: Traditional Thali
info: A massive platter offering a balanced meal with different flavors: sweet, salt, bitter, sour, astringent, and spicy.
history: The concept of a Thali is rooted in Ayurveda, which advocates for eating all six tastes in a single meal to maintain a healthy body.
trivia: A typical grand Rajasthani or Gujarati Thali can have over 20 different small dishes served in 'katoris' (small bowls)!
funFact: In many traditional restaurants, waiters use hand signals to communicate exactly which vegetable or bread needs refilling without making a sound.

name: Hyderabadi Biryani
info: A royal, fragrant mixed rice dish made with basmati rice, spices, and heavily marinated meat.
history: Originated in the kitchens of the Nizam of Hyderabad, blending Mughal and Iranian cuisine with local Telugu spices.
trivia: It is cooked using the 'Dum' method, where the cooking pot is sealed with dough so no steam can escape, trapping all the flavors.
funFact: Legend says Biryani was invented by Mumtaz Mahal (the lady for whom the Taj Mahal was built) to feed undernourished soldiers!

name: Masala Dosa
info: A thin, crispy, savory crepe made from a fermented batter of lentils and rice, usually stuffed with a potato curry.
history: Traced back to the Udupi region of Karnataka, it is one of the most ancient dishes of South India.
trivia: Fermenting the batter overnight naturally breaks down starches and enhances its nutritional value and digestibility.
funFact: In 2012, a restaurant in Hyderabad made a Guinness World Record by preparing a Masala Dosa that was a staggering 54 feet long!

name: Chole Bhature
info: A heavy, spicy, and irresistible dish consisting of spicy chickpea curry (Chole) and large, fluffy fried bread (Bhatura).
history: It emerged as a staple street food in Northern India, particularly in Delhi and Punjab, post-independence.
trivia: It is traditionally served with raw onions, pickles, and a tall glass of cold, sweet Lassi to balance the heavy spices.
funFact: Virat Kohli, the famous Indian cricketer, has famously declared Ram's Chole Bhature in Delhi as his ultimate cheat day meal!

name: Samosa
info: A ubiquitous deep-fried pastry with a savory filling, typically spiced potatoes, onions, and peas.
history: Surprisingly, the Samosa did not originate in India! It traveled from the Middle East (where it was called 'Sambosa') via trade routes.
trivia: While the potato filling is standard today, historical records show ancient royal samosas were filled with minced meat, nuts, and dry fruits.
funFact: It is scientifically designed in a tetrahedral shape so it cooks evenly when deep-fried!

name: Rasgulla / Roshogolla
info: A syrupy dessert made from ball-shaped dumplings of chhena (an Indian cottage cheese) and semolina dough.
history: There was a famous, intense legal battle between West Bengal and Odisha over the origin of this sweet, with both getting regional GI tags!
trivia: The sweet is extremely spongy; a perfectly made Rasgulla will regain its round shape immediately after being squeezed tightly.
funFact: It was traditionally offered to Goddess Lakshmi at the Jagannath Temple to appease her when Lord Jagannath went on his chariot journey without her!
